suite.name: Recorded

kw.name: Open Bench
kw.msg: Set suite metadata 'Radio' to value 'Connect Systems CS7000-PLUS (cs7000p)'.
Set suite metadata 'Hardware' to value 'Connect Systems CS7000-PLUS'.
Set suite metadata 'Calibration' to value 'assumed, measured 2026-10-20 (d55ce4aa0a3c)'.
Set suite metadata 'Suite commit' to value '2bd5f60a1c'.
kw.doc: Load the bench, its calibration and the radio file, and prepare the instruments. All five are mandatory and differ from tester to tester, so suites take them from the command line (-v BENCH:... and so on). `firmware` names what the radio runs, such as a git describe; `hardware` names the unit, by model and serial number, since units of one model measure differently. `dsp` names the DSP image the radio's audio processor runs, such as its sha256; it is mandatory for radio files with dsp_image: true, whose firmware states can differ in it alone.

test.name: 70cm: APRS Recording Frames Heard

kw.name: Use Band
kw.doc: Make a band from the radio file current: captures and transmissions use its frequency. Sets ${BAND} and ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} for the test. oat.expand calls it in each per-band test's setup.

kw.name: Operator Does
kw.arg: Check the transmitter is cabled to the radio through the attenuators with no antenna connected, and set the radio to APRS on ${FREQUENCY_MHZ} MHz with its TNC port connected
kw.doc: Ask the operator to do something and wait until it's done.

kw.name: Split String
kw.doc: Splits the `string` using `separator` as a delimiter string.

kw.name: Play Aprs Recording
kw.msg: t1.wav at 3000 Hz: 37 of 95 reference frames (38.9%), 0 the reference didn't have, 0 not UI frames
kw.doc: Play a recording of off-air APRS traffic (a 16-bit WAV) as FM on the test frequency and score what the radio's TNC reported against `reference`, Dire Wolf's atest output for the same file. The track's peak deviates the carrier by deviation_hz; nothing is pre-emphasized, so play a flat (discriminator) track. start_s and duration_s play part of the track, scored against the reference frames that ended in it. The recordings carry real callsigns: cabled bench only, no antenna. Returns the counts and the fraction of the reference heard.

test.doc: APRS-REC-1: the fraction of the reference decoder's frames the radio reports, at each deviation.

kw.name: Close Bench
kw.doc: Stop the instruments and write measurements.json: every capture, check and operator answer, with the run's provenance. Absolute paths are made relative, so the file can be published as it is.

suite.doc:
APRS receive against a recording of real traffic: the transmitter plays the track as FM, the radio reports every frame it decodes on its KISS TNC, and the count is compared with what Dire Wolf's atest decodes from the same file. See docs/aprs-recorded-benchmark.md for the track, the reference file and the wiring.
The recording carries real callsigns and its author asks that it never be played over the air: run this only with the transmitter cabled to the radio through the attenuators, no antenna anywhere. Results are recorded for comparison; there is no limit yet.
